facts.text: Colonel Marcelo Usera’s family gave the neighborhood its name, with streets like Isabelita, Amparo, and Gabriel Usera honoring relatives and service personnel.
Since the 2000s, Usera has become Madrid’s Chinatown, hosting nearly 11,000 Chinese residents who bring vibrant festivals and cuisine.
The Caja Mágica stadium in Usera stages the annual Madrid Open, a top‑tier ATP World Tour Masters 1000 tennis event.
Inside Usera Metro station, a hidden indoor market lets visitors sample traditional Spanish foods and crafts right where the trains arrive.
Okuda’s Gallery, officially called “Factory of Dreams,” is Usera’s most high‑profile art space, though it’s not always open, so check before visiting.
Usera lies south of Madrid’s center, bordered east by the Manzanares River, south by the M‑40 motorway, and west by the A‑42 autovía.
